holidays.name: National Drink Wine Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to uncorking a bottle and raising a glass, whether it's a bold red, a crisp white, or a sparkling bubbly. Wine lovers around the country swirl, sniff, and sip while pretending to detect notes of 'blackberry and leather.'
holidays.origin: An unofficial food-and-drink observance popularized by wine enthusiasts and the beverage industry, listed on many national day calendars. Its exact founder is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Archaeologists have found evidence of wine production in Georgia dating back about 8,000 years, making it one of the oldest known alcoholic beverages still enjoyed today.

holidays.name: National Crab Stuffed Flounder Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the delightfully layered seafood dish in which a flaky flounder fillet is wrapped around or topped with a rich, buttery crab-meat stuffing. It's basically a fish hugging a crab.
holidays.origin: Part of the many unofficial national food days observed on social media and food calendars, with the exact origin unknown. The dish is a classic of Mid-Atlantic and Chesapeake Bay cooking.
holidays.funFact: Flounder are born with an eye on each side of the head, but as they mature one eye migrates across the skull so both end up on the same side of the body.

holidays.name: Pluto Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the little planet-turned-dwarf-planet that could. Space fans celebrate the discovery of Pluto with themed parties, memes, and heated debates about whether it deserves its planet status back.
holidays.origin: Pluto was discovered on February 18, 1930, by astronomer Clyde Tombaugh at Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona, after he compared photographic plates of the night sky.
holidays.funFact: Pluto's name was suggested by an 11-year-old English schoolgirl named Venetia Burney, who was inspired by the Roman god of the underworld.

holidays.name: Thumb Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day to give a big thumbs up to the humble opposable thumb, which makes texting, gripping, hitchhiking, and high-fiving possible. Participants are encouraged to thank their thumbs for all their hard work.
holidays.origin: A lighthearted unofficial observance with no clear founder, spread through novelty holiday listings that encourage people to celebrate the body part that separates us from many other animals.
holidays.funFact: The thumb has its own set of muscles and gives humans the precision grip that is crucial for using tools, and some primates like the koala have even evolved extra opposable digits.

holidays.name: National Battery Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the little power sources that run remote controls, flashlights, toys, and phones. It's also a nudge to recycle old batteries properly rather than hiding them in the junk drawer.
holidays.origin: Observed on February 18 in honor of the birthday of Alessandro Volta, the Italian physicist who invented the first chemical battery, the voltaic pile, around 1800.
holidays.funFact: The unit of electric potential, the volt, is named after Alessandro Volta, so every time you check a voltage you're quietly name-dropping him.
